overall: The AG found no Open Meeting Law violation on any of the three allegations: the scheduling calls were excluded from deliberation, pre-meeting deliberation was not proven, and the notice's pay-equity topic was specific enough to cover the alternative motion.

allegations.summary: Three commissioners allegedly deliberated after the Dec. 10, 2012 meeting to schedule a special meeting for Dec. 17, 2012, without the Chair.
allegations.key_passage: This type of communication is explicitly excluded from the definition of deliberation.

allegations.summary: Before the Dec. 17, 2012 meeting, a commissioner allegedly distributed a written motion and began discussing it with other members, constituting unlawful deliberation.
allegations.key_passage: We are unable to determine which account is more credible.

allegations.summary: The Dec. 17, 2012 notice allegedly omitted an anticipated topic: a commissioner's alternative pay-increase motion that was considered at the meeting.
allegations.key_passage: However, the notice was clear as to the topic the Commission would discuss, and that topic was sufficient to include any discussion or motions that could be made.
